title: Platelet count–volume interactions do not improve frozen HbA1c prediction across two NHANES recruitment cohorts
abstract: Platelet size–count relationships may carry glycemic information omitted by separate platelet indices. We tested a25-term platelet count by mean platelet volume spline surface beyond flexible additive conventional predictors, including fasting glucose and separate CBC indices. Models trained on NHANES2011–2012 (n=2279) were frozen and evaluated on separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=2360). Weighted HbA1c MSE increased from 0.244020 to 0.254382 percentage-points squared; delta +0.010362, joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [+0.001256,+0.210144]. This representation failed its incremental-improvement criterion. Clipping and influence checks attenuated deterioration. Instrument changes and repeated author exposure limit interpretation. These results concern one predictive representation, not absence of platelet–glycemia biology or clinical utility.
